text: of rejection epi- sodes without increased toxicity.4,5,18-21 Alemtuzumab has also been used, but data for this drug are comparatively limited.19,22,23 Some consider the interleukin-2 receptor antibodies to be the first-line choice for induction therapy because of their superior safety profile. While there appears to be no differ- ence between rabbit antilymphocyte immunoglobulins and interleukin-2 receptor antibodies in terms of efficacy, acute rejection in high-risk patients appears to occur less 1814 Immunosuppressants often with rabbit antilymphocyte immunoglobulins, which may be the preferred choice in patients who are highly sen- sitised or receiving a second transplant.19 Basiliximab or daclizumab, used as part of a ciclosporin-based regimen, are recommended in the UK as options for induction ther- apy in children and adolescents undergoing renal trans- plantation, irrespective of immunological risk.14 As immunosuppressant regimens have developed the role of corticosteroids has come to be questioned, mainly be- cause of the adverse effects associated with their pro- longed use.4,9,24,25 Studies indicate that corticosteroid withdrawal is feasible in many patients initially given tri- ple therapy,1,26 although there is debate about the long- term consequences of this for graft survival.4,25,27,28 Corti- costeroid-sparing regimens may increase the risk of acute or chronic rejection, and the benefit associated with them may be limited by the high proportion of patients who need to resume corticosteroid therapy. Nevertheless, such regimens are considered to be feasible, even in the early period after transplantation. Even complete avoidance of corticosteroids may be possible with induction therapy us- ing interleukin-2 receptor antibodies. However, it is crucial to individualise therapy, and caution is advised for high- risk patients, such as African Americans, sensitised, previ- ously transplanted patients, or those with previous acute rejection episodes. Some consider the best approach to rapid corticosteroid withdrawal to be induction therapy (with antilymphocyte immunoglobulins in high-risk pa- tients), calcineurin inhibitors, and mycophenolate mofet- il.25 Protocols that withdraw, minimise, or avoid cal- cineurin inhibitors have also been investigated.28-33 Ciclosporin withdrawal is considered by some30 to be more feasible for patients treated with mycophenolate mofetil than those given azathioprine.
